excerpt: The oldest layer of Hindu scripture, the Rigveda was composed and transmitted orally in Vedic Sanskrit, anchoring Hindu ritual and cosmology.
Central to Jewish identity, the Exodus narrative and the giving of the Law at Sinai establish the covenant between God and Israel.
Zoroaster preached a dualist cosmos of truth versus falsehood under the god Ahura Mazda, influencing later monotheisms.
Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment and taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path as the way out of suffering.
Confucius taught an ethics of ren (benevolence) and li (ritual propriety) that shaped Chinese governance and society for millennia.
The crucifixion and reported resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth became the foundation of Christian faith and the New Testament.
Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina marks year one of the Islamic calendar and the founding of the first Muslim community.
Mutual excommunications split Christianity into the Roman Catholic West and Eastern Orthodox churches over authority and doctrine.
Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses challenged indulgences and papal authority, fracturing Western Christianity and reshaping Europe.
